Frequently Asked Questions

Are the AI tool prices on this website official?

We use provider pricing pages and official help documentation as references. Prices can change, so each comparison links to the official source for a final check.

Are prices the same in every country?

Not always. Regional pricing, taxes, currency conversion, app-store billing and local availability can affect the amount shown at checkout.

Does Editsfield AI sell subscriptions?

No. This is an independent information website. Use the official provider links on each guide to view plans and subscribe directly.

How do I choose the right AI tool?

Start with your task, compare free limits and paid features, then check output quality, usage caps, privacy terms and cancellation rules.

Can I suggest a tool for this directory?

Yes. Use the Submit a New AI Tool Guide page to suggest a tool or send a correction.

About Editsfield AI

Clear, practical guidance for choosing AI tools

Editsfield AI is an independent informational website published by Editsfield AI. We help readers understand AI products, compare features and plans, explore practical use cases, and find official resources before deciding which tools may suit their needs.

Why we created Editsfield AI

AI products are changing quickly. New tools, subscription tiers, features, usage limits and integrations can make it difficult to understand what a service offers and whether it fits a particular task or budget.

We created Editsfield AI to organize this information into accessible guides. Our aim is to make research easier to follow—not to tell every reader to buy the same product. Different tools serve different purposes, and the right choice depends on what someone wants to accomplish, their budget, location and workflow.

What you can find on this website

AI chatbots and assistants

Guides to conversational AI assistants, their capabilities, plan differences and common uses for research, writing and everyday tasks.

AI pricing and plans

Explanations of free and paid tiers, subscription features, billing details and usage limits, with links to official provider information where available.

Image generation

Information about AI image tools, their creative features, editing options and differences that readers may want to consider.

Video generation

Guides to AI video products, generation workflows, supported capabilities and plan considerations.

Practical comparisons

Side-by-side explanations that help readers understand differences between products rather than relying on unsupported rankings.

How-to guides and updates

Explanations of features, workflows and product changes intended to help readers use AI services more confidently.

How we research and prepare our guides

We aim to make our articles useful, understandable and transparent about the information they contain. When preparing or updating a guide, our editorial approach is to:

  • Consult official product pages, pricing pages, help centres and documentation when researching product details.
  • Explain plan names, features, limits and availability in context instead of assuming every feature is available to every user.
  • Distinguish provider-published information from our own explanations, comparisons and general observations.
  • Include relevant source links so readers can check important details with the product provider.
  • Review content when we identify a significant product change or receive a credible correction.

Product information can change after an article is published. Prices, features, usage limits and availability may differ by country, currency, account type or billing period. We encourage readers to confirm purchase and subscription details on the provider's official website before making a decision.

Our editorial standards

We want readers to be able to understand what our guides do—and do not—claim. We aim to:

  • Use clear language and organize information around real reader questions.
  • Avoid fabricated product features, invented prices, fake testimonials, unsupported performance claims and made-up statistics.
  • Identify uncertainty when information may be incomplete, regional or subject to change.
  • Correct material errors when they are brought to our attention and can be verified.
  • Make the independent nature of this website clear and distinguish editorial information from advertising or disclosed commercial links.

Our guides are informational resources. They are not a guarantee that a particular AI product will meet every reader's expectations or requirements.

Independent website and brand ownership

Editsfield AI is published by Editsfield AI as an independent information resource. We are not an official website of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Midjourney, Runway, ElevenLabs or any other AI product provider discussed in our articles, and we do not claim to represent those companies.

Product names, company names, logos and trademarks belong to their respective owners. We use relevant names to identify and discuss products. Their appearance on this website does not imply endorsement, sponsorship or an official partnership.

Advertising and how this website is supported

Operating and maintaining an informational website takes time and resources. This website may display third-party advertising, including Google AdSense advertisements, where enabled. Advertising helps support the publication and maintenance of our guides.

Advertisements are delivered by advertising providers and are separate from our editorial content. Their appearance does not mean that we recommend or endorse the advertised product or service. If we publish sponsored material or use affiliate links, we aim to identify those relationships clearly. Please also read our Privacy Policy and Disclaimer for further information.

Corrections, suggestions and reader feedback

Reader feedback helps us identify unclear explanations, outdated information and broken links. If you notice an error in a guide, have a question about something we published or want to suggest an AI topic for coverage, please contact us. Where possible, include the article URL and a link to the relevant official product information so the issue can be reviewed.

We cannot provide account-specific technical support, process refunds, change subscriptions or access accounts for third-party AI services. For those matters, contact the relevant provider directly.

Contact Editsfield AI

Explore our website

Browse our AI chatbot guides, AI image generation guides, AI video generation guides and individual AI pricing articles to learn more about the tools covered on this website.

Cursor AI Code Editor Guide 2026: Agent, Features, Plans & Pricing

Cursor is an AI-powered code editor designed to help developers understand repositories, write and edit code, debug problems and complete larger development tasks with an AI agent.

Visit official Cursor ↗Official plans & pricing ↗
Reviewed November 14, 2026 · Product, plan and documentation references checked against official Cursor sources · Independent guide
CU
Quick answer: Who should try Cursor?

Cursor is worth exploring if you want an editor where AI can understand project context and help with multi-file implementation—not just autocomplete. Use Ask to understand code, Plan to outline a larger change and Agent to implement it. Review the diff, commands and tests before accepting the result.

Important pricing update: Cursor's current official pricing documentation lists Free, Plus, Premium, Super and Ultra plans as part of The X Subscription. Older articles may still show Cursor Pro and Pro+ prices; Cursor says those are legacy plans that continue for existing subscribers. The current prices below were checked November 14, 2026.

What is Cursor?

Cursor is an AI-focused code editor for software development. It combines familiar editor workflows with codebase-aware AI assistance, inline completions and an Agent that can search files, edit code across a project and run terminal commands. It is intended to support a developer's workflow, not replace code review, testing or engineering judgment.

What can Cursor actually do?

Tab autocomplete and edits

Predicts code as you type and can suggest multi-line edits, helping reduce repetitive typing. Review suggestions for correctness and consistency.

Ask and codebase context

Ask questions about a repository, find relevant files and understand existing implementations before making changes.

Agent mode

Give Agent a task in plain language. It can inspect the codebase, edit multiple files, run terminal commands, fix errors and help verify the result.

Plan and multi-step work

Use a plan for larger features or migrations so you can inspect the approach before implementation proceeds.

Rules, skills and MCP

Customize project instructions and connect external tools or services through Model Context Protocol integrations.

Cloud Agents and automations

Eligible paid plans add cloud-based agent workflows and automations for work that can run beyond the local editor session.

Common Cursor use cases

  • Web development: build and refine React, Next.js and other frontend/backend features.
  • Mobile development: assist with Flutter, React Native and native project code while you validate builds on the target toolchain.
  • Debugging: trace errors across files, propose fixes and run relevant commands or tests.
  • Refactoring: reorganize code, improve readability and update repeated patterns across a repository.
  • Learning an unfamiliar project: ask for explanations of architecture, functions, dependencies and data flow.
  • Tool-connected workflows: connect supported services using MCP, with permissions limited to what the task needs.

Cursor plans and pricing

The current official plan documentation lists these individual plans. Prices are in USD and exclude applicable taxes. Cursor describes paid plans as having a weekly usage pool shared across Cursor and Grok; higher tiers include larger pools.

Free

$0/month

Limited Agent and Chat usage. Suitable for trying the editor and checking whether the workflow fits your projects.

Plus

$8/month

Base shared usage pool and included Cursor/Grok features. The current documentation says only Grok models are available on this tier; third-party models are not included.

Annual: $80/year.

Premium

$30/month

4× Plus usage, Cloud Agents and automations, Origin code hosting, Bugbot code reviews and third-party models billed at API list price.

Annual: $300/year.

Super

$100/month

15× Plus usage and priority model access at peak times, with Premium features.

Annual: $1,000/year.

Ultra

$200/month

50× Plus usage and earliest access to new products and models, with Super features.

Annual: $2,000/year.

Teams and Enterprise

$30–$200 / seat

Teams tiers are listed at $30, $100 or $200 per seat/month; Enterprise pricing is custom. Designed for organization-level administration and pooled usage.

Understand the usage and billing model: The included usage pool refreshes weekly and is shared across Cursor and Grok. Third-party model use is not included in the displayed subscription price; on Premium and above it is billed separately at API list price from prepaid credit. Grok API usage is also billed separately at standard model rates. Annual prices and taxes can change, so verify the checkout total before paying.

Which Cursor plan may fit your workflow?

Your usagePlan to investigateReason
Learning the editor or occasional coding questionsFreeTry the core experience before paying.
Light use of included Cursor modelsPlusLower-cost paid entry tier with a base usage pool.
Regular Agent work and cloud workflowsPremiumAdds larger usage, Cloud Agents, automations, Origin and Bugbot.
Heavy daily useSuperProvides 15× Plus usage and priority model access at peak times.
Very high usage or multiple agent workflowsUltraProvides 50× Plus usage and earliest access to new products and models.
Shared controls for a development organizationTeams / EnterpriseOrganization-focused billing, administration and security features.

What to test before paying

  1. Open a real project. Use a repository you understand, with a working Git history and clear build instructions.
  2. Ask for an explanation first. Check whether Cursor correctly identifies the architecture, entry points and dependencies.
  3. Try a small feature. Give Agent one bounded task with clear acceptance criteria rather than asking for a full application at once.
  4. Inspect every change. Review diffs, new packages, file deletions, generated secrets and terminal commands.
  5. Run project checks. Execute tests, linting, type checks and a production build yourself.
  6. Track usage. Compare the subscription allowance and any third-party model charges with the value you actually get.

Practical test prompt

“First inspect this repository and explain its architecture. Do not edit files yet. Identify the files that control the login form and explain how validation currently works. Then propose a small, testable improvement and list the files you would change. Wait for my approval before implementing it.”

This prompt tests whether the editor can understand a project before making changes. After reviewing the plan, ask it to implement one small improvement and run the relevant tests.

Limitations and things to consider

StrengthsLimitations / checks
Agent can search a repository, edit multiple files and run terminal commands.Generated changes can be wrong, incomplete or introduce regressions; review and test them.
Codebase context can help explain unfamiliar projects.Indexing and context do not guarantee that every file or dependency is understood correctly.
MCP and project rules can extend workflows.Connected tools may access external systems; review permissions before enabling them.
Multiple subscription tiers support different usage levels.Weekly pools, third-party model charges, legacy plans and taxes can make billing less obvious.

Privacy and code security

Cursor's privacy documentation says Privacy Mode can prevent code data from being used for training by Cursor or its model providers. Prompts and relevant code context are still sent to model providers for processing to deliver AI features. Before using Cursor with private client repositories or proprietary code, review the current privacy documentation, configure Privacy Mode and follow your organization's security policy. Do not paste passwords, API keys or production credentials into prompts.

Frequently asked questions

Is Cursor free?

Yes. Cursor lists a Free plan with limited Agent and Chat usage. Check the official plan page for current limits.

Is Cursor the same as VS Code?

Cursor is a separate AI-focused code editor built around familiar editor workflows. Its main distinction is its integrated AI assistance, codebase context and Agent workflows.

Can Cursor build a complete app?

It can help plan and implement features across a codebase, but a developer still needs to define requirements, review changes, run tests and verify the finished application.

Does Cursor support MCP?

Yes. Cursor documents MCP integrations for connecting external tools and data sources. Review each server's permissions before connecting it.

Why do some websites show Cursor Pro at $20/month?

Those may describe older legacy subscriptions. Cursor's current model-and-pricing documentation lists Free, Plus, Premium, Super and Ultra, and says existing legacy plans continue to work.

Are third-party AI models included?

They are not included in the displayed subscription usage pool. Cursor says third-party models are available at API list price on Premium and higher plans, billed separately from prepaid credit.

Where should I confirm current prices?

Use Cursor's official pricing page and model-pricing documentation before subscribing. Prices, plan names and feature allowances can change.

ElevenLabs Review & Pricing 2026: AI Voice, Text to Speech and Dubbing

ElevenLabs is an AI audio platform for natural-sounding text-to-speech, voice design and cloning, speech-to-text, dubbing, sound effects and music. This guide explains which features matter for creators, developers and teams—and what the current plans include.

Quick answer: Who should use ElevenLabs?

Choose ElevenLabs when spoken audio is the main deliverable: narration for YouTube videos, audiobooks, podcasts, multilingual dubbing, character voices or speech inside an app. Its strongest value is the combination of expressive voice generation, voice tools and production workflows—not simply converting a short sentence into audio.

Promotions, annual billing, taxes, regional availability and credit consumption can change. What is ElevenLabs?

ElevenLabs develops generative audio models and tools. Its creator-facing platform combines text-to-speech, voice design, voice cloning, speech-to-text, voice changing, sound effects, music, dubbing and Studio-style production. Developers can also use APIs and SDKs to add speech and audio features to applications.

Interface screenshot: ElevenLabs official documentation. Studio interface may vary by account, plan and product updates.

Key features and workflows

Text to Speech

Turn scripts into spoken narration, with controls for voice selection and delivery. Useful for explainers, tutorials, audiobooks and product demos.

Voice Design & Library

Find an existing voice or design a voice from a description. Test pronunciation, pacing and emotional tone using the actual script before committing to a long render.

Voice Cloning

Instant Voice Cloning starts on Starter; Professional Voice Cloning is available from Creator and requires voice verification. Only clone voices you own or are authorized to use.

Dubbing & Speech Tools

Translate and dub audio, transcribe speech, change voices and build multilingual versions of existing content. Review names, timing and translation accuracy manually.

Sound Effects & Music

Generate supporting audio assets as part of the wider ElevenCreative workflow. Check the relevant model, credits and usage terms for each output type.

Studio & API

Studio supports longer-form audio production such as narration and audiobooks; APIs and SDKs let developers integrate audio generation into their products.

ElevenLabs pricing and plans

The official monthly pricing page currently lists the following USD plans and monthly credit allowances:

$0 / month

  • Sound Effects, Voice Design and Music
  • 3 Studio projects
  • Personal use; no commercial license

  • Instant Voice Cloning
  • 20 Studio projects
  • Dubbing Studio and image/video features

Enterprise pricing is custom. The amount of audio generated from a credit allowance depends on the model and task, so do not treat credits as a fixed number of finished minutes across every feature. Check the official live pricing comparison before subscribing.

Which plan makes sense?

  • Testing: Start with Free to evaluate voice quality and pronunciation; do not use it as a commercial publishing license.
  • Monetized solo creator: Starter is the entry point for commercial use and Instant Voice Cloning.
  • Consistent personal voice: Creator adds Professional Voice Cloning and a much larger monthly allowance.
  • Heavy production or teams: Compare Pro, Scale and Business against actual monthly usage, seats and API needs.

How to evaluate ElevenLabs for a real video workflow

For a creator making explainers, test a full paragraph rather than a single demo sentence. Include Urdu names, English technical terms, dates and numbers, then compare the generated narration with the intended delivery. Listen for pronunciation, pauses, emphasis, consistency and audio artifacts before editing the video.

Limitations and important checks

  • Pronunciation and emotional delivery are not perfect on every script; manually review names, Urdu/Roman Urdu text, acronyms and numbers.
  • Credit use depends on the model and feature. Long scripts, retries, dubbing and other tools can consume the allowance quickly.
  • Voice clones remain account-based assets; they are not simply downloadable standalone model files.
  • Professional Voice Cloning is restricted to your own verified voice. Do not clone another person without the required authorization and compliance with provider rules.
  • Commercial rights, attribution and allowed uses depend on the plan and terms in effect when the output is generated.

Practical test prompt

Use this short test to evaluate narration quality with a real technology-explainer style:

Read this as a confident, natural technology documentary narrator. Keep the delivery clear and conversational, with a short pause after each sentence. Do not sound like a news anchor or use exaggerated drama. Preserve every technical term, number and name exactly. Script: “In 1970, the Apollo 13 crew faced a dangerous problem. Carbon dioxide was building up inside the spacecraft. The solution had to be built from the limited materials available on board.”

What to check in the result

  • Does the voice sound natural without robotic pacing?
  • Are technical words and numbers pronounced correctly?
  • Can pauses and emphasis be adjusted without regenerating everything?
  • Is the exported audio clean and suitable for editing?
  • How many credits did the complete script consume?

Frequently asked questions

Does ElevenLabs have a free plan?

Yes. The current pricing page lists 10,000 monthly credits on Free. It is intended for testing and personal use, not commercial publishing.

Which ElevenLabs plan includes voice cloning?

Instant Voice Cloning starts on Starter. Professional Voice Cloning starts on Creator and requires verification of your own voice.

Can I use ElevenLabs audio in monetized YouTube videos?

Commercial use is included on paid plans for eligible outputs, subject to the current terms and your rights to the input material. The Free plan does not include a commercial license.

Is ElevenLabs useful for Urdu narration?

Test your exact Urdu or Roman Urdu script and the selected model before relying on it. Pronunciation, language support and naturalness can vary by model and voice.

Notebook, AI Studio and developer workflows

Custom lyrics and vocals

Extend, cover and remix

Continue a song, explore alternate versions or adjust its direction. Results can vary, so keep the original project and compare versions.

Upload and transform audio

Stem separation

Suno Studio

Which Suno plan should you choose?

  • Explore ideas: Free is suitable for personal experiments and learning the prompt workflow.
  • Publish monetized creator content: Pro is the entry paid plan with commercial-use rights for eligible songs created while subscribed.
  • Produce frequently: Premier adds four times the monthly credits of Pro, more downloads and Suno Studio.

Commercial use, ownership and copyright

This distinction is important. Suno says songs created on the Free plan are for personal, non-commercial use. Songs created while subscribed to Pro or Premier are granted commercial-use rights, subject to the terms. Suno also explains that a paid subscription does not automatically grant commercial rights retroactively to older Free-plan songs. If a track matters commercially, check its creation date, subscription status, download eligibility and the current terms.

Commercial-use permission does not guarantee that an AI-generated song qualifies for copyright protection in your country. Copyright rules differ by jurisdiction and may require meaningful human authorship. Keep records of your original lyrics, prompts, edits and source material, and do not upload copyrighted songs or lyrics unless you have the necessary rights.

Practical test prompt

Use the same brief each time you compare versions. This example is aimed at a short creator-video background track rather than a full pop song:

Create a 35-second instrumental background track for a serious but engaging technology-history documentary. Mood: curious, tense and gradually hopeful. Style: cinematic electronic documentary score with soft analog synth pulses, restrained low percussion, warm piano notes and subtle strings. Start minimal, build gently after 12 seconds, reach a small emotional lift near the end, then finish with a clean resolved ending. No vocals, no lyrics, no spoken words, no sound effects, no recognizable existing melody. Keep the music supportive and leave space for voice-over.

What to check in the result

  • Does the generated track follow the requested mood and instrumental-only instruction?
  • Does the arrangement build naturally without overpowering narration?
  • Is the ending clean, or does it stop abruptly?
  • Can you edit or separate the parts you need on your plan?
  • Record credits used, generation attempts, duration, download availability and plan.

Limitations and things to verify

  • Prompt adherence is not guaranteed: unwanted vocals, extra sections or abrupt endings may appear.
  • Music generation is probabilistic. Repeated prompts can produce noticeably different songs.
  • Free-plan songs are not licensed for monetized use; upgrading later does not normally make old Free outputs commercial automatically.
  • Commercial-use rights do not guarantee copyright registration or protection in every country.
  • Before uploading, check for unlicensed lyrics, samples, melodies, voice likenesses or source recordings.

Frequently asked questions

Is Suno free to use?

Yes. The Free plan currently provides 50 credits per day, but it does not include monthly downloads or commercial-use rights.

Can I monetize Suno songs on YouTube?

Suno grants commercial-use rights for eligible songs created while subscribed to Pro or Premier. Free-plan songs are non-commercial. Check the terms and keep proof of your subscription and track creation period.

If I upgrade, do my old Free songs become commercial?

Not automatically. Suno says a paid subscription does not normally grant retroactive commercial rights to songs created on the Free plan.

What is the difference between Pro and Premier?

Pro includes 2,500 credits and 20 monthly downloads. Premier includes 10,000 credits, 60 monthly downloads and Suno Studio with additional production features.
